content: Have you ever wondered why a 100-acre farm today produces three times more wheat than it did 50 years ago? The sun is the same, the rain is similar, but the food on our plates has multiplied. What changed?

Imagine you are a farmer with a small piece of land. The population of your town is doubling every year. How would you feed everyone without buying more land? Would you plant more seeds? Use better soil? Predict what you would do.

content.title: The Crop Yield Equation
content.description: Visualizing how improved seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation combine to multiply yield.

content: The answer lies in Agricultural Improvement. It involves three major scientific approaches: 1. Crop Variety Improvement (better seeds), 2. Crop Production Management (better nurturing), and 3. Crop Protection Management (saving from pests).

description: The period when agricultural productivity increased drastically due to new technologies.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main approaches to improving crop yields?

content: Reflection time: Think about your last meal. If farmers stopped using modern techniques, how much of that meal would still be on your plate? Try explaining this to a friend.
Connection: Improvement in food resources connects directly to Ecosystem Balance and Human Health. Without enough food, society cannot function, but too much chemical fertilizer harms the Earth.
Mastery Challenge: Design a sustainable farm for your town. Choose 2 crops that grow in different seasons (Kharif and Rabi) and explain how you will protect them from pests naturally.
